arrangement.description: Seven Gate 32-bar arrangement. Parts are placed in 8-bar sections. Tempo and meter stay on the conductor.

cycles: Primary A groups 7 sixteenth notes, 1680 ticks. Seven bars hold 112 sixteenths, and 112 divides by 7, so the cycle meets the downbeat again at bar 8. The part ends after the first bar of the next pass. Meter stays 4/4.
Secondary A waits one sixteenth, then groups 5. Five bars realign that delayed grid. The wait is not a meter change.
Bass A sounds three sixteenths and rests the fourth. That group resets every bar because 4 sixteenths fill one beat, four times.
Drums A reset every bar. Motif A resets every 2 bars. The harmonic field changes every 2 bars.
departures: Primary B has one G4 (67) at tick 5160. G is outside E Phrygian dominant. It is one attack, then the line returns.
kits.identity: Seven Gate locks a 7-sixteenth primary sequence to a 4-on-the-floor kit and a 3-note bass group. Variation B drops the kick to half time, moves the lead onto a late eighth grid, and answers with a two-note secondary.
kits.limitations: Play variation A parts together, or variation B parts together. The arrangement is the only place those sets trade. Odd groups do not change the 4/4 bar.
kits.title: Seven Gate

cycles: Primary A groups 5 sixteenth notes, 1200 ticks. Five bars hold 80 sixteenths, so the cycle meets the downbeat at bar 6. The 8-bar part then carries 3 bars of the next pass. Meter stays 4/4.
Secondary A groups 3 sixteenth notes. Sixteen sixteenths leave a remainder of 1, so the group does not reset each bar. It resets every 3 bars, where 48 sixteenths divide by 3.
Bass A is the offbeat eighth, one bar long. Drums A gallop inside the bar. The field changes every bar.
departures: Primary B bar 8, tick 28320, is Bb4 (70) for 200 ticks.
Secondary B bar 8, tick 28800, is Bb4 (70) for 1000 ticks. These two notes do not overlap. Bb is outside A harmonic minor.
kits.identity: Fifth Lattice starts on the secondary sequence and a galloping kick. The primary line is a 5-step lattice that enters later. Variation B answers in quarters and flags one Bb.
kits.limitations: The opening eight bars have no primary sequence and no motif. That silence is written. It is not a missing file. Bb is a departure, not a new key.
kits.title: Fifth Lattice

cycles: Primary A groups 9 sixteenth notes, 2160 ticks, and sounds 120 ticks after each selected step. Nine and 16 are coprime, so the group does not reset inside one bar. It would meet the downbeat every 9 bars. The part ends at bar 8, and the cycle resets only when the part starts again. Meter stays 4/4.
Secondary A waits 360 ticks, then groups 5 sixteenths. That late grid realigns every 5 bars. The wait does not move the bar line, and it does not copy the primary 9-step.
Motif A places one attack every 2160 ticks, the same 9-sixteenth span, and resets with the part.
The field holds 4 bars, then 4 bars. Drums A reset every bar on a shifted hat grid.
departures: Primary B bar 6, tick 21120, is G4 (67) for 1440 ticks. G is outside F Phrygian.
kits.identity: Nine Pulse shifts a 9-step primary by 120 ticks and hangs a 4-bar field under it. The bass enters only at bar 9 of the arrangement. Variation B is three held attacks per bar plus one G.
kits.limitations: The 120-tick phase sits inside the sixteenth grid. It does not move the downbeat. The 9-step cycle does not finish inside the 8-bar part.
kits.title: Nine Pulse

cycles: Primary A attacks on groups of 3, 3, and 2 sixteenths, then the same groups again. The sum is 16 sixteenths, so the pattern resets every bar. The bar remains 3840 ticks and the meter remains 4/4.
Drums A place the kick on the tresillo eighths, which is the same 3+3+2 shape in eighth notes, and that also resets every bar.
Secondary A resets every bar. Motif A alternates even and odd bars. The field staggers inside the bar and restarts each bar in variation A.
departures: Primary B bar 8, tick 30480, is C#5 (73) for 150 ticks. C# is outside B Phrygian.
kits.identity: Return Spiral builds the bar as 3+3+2 sixteenths, twice. The kick follows that tresillo. Variation B moves the lead to the off-sixteenths and flags one C#.
kits.limitations: 3+3+2+3+3+2 equals 16 sixteenths, so the odd groups reset every bar. They do not create a new meter. C# is one attack at the end of variation B.
kits.title: Return Spiral

note_policy: Note-only MIDI. No program changes, controllers, pitch bend, or sound-design messages.
odd_step: Odd-step grouping is a local cycle. It does not change the 4/4 meter. A bar stays 3840 ticks.

preview_excerpt.reason: The 32-bar arrangement is longer than 40 seconds, so the primary preview is the first 16 bars.

range_statement: Drums use MIDI channel index 9, the GM channel 10, and only the mapped pitches 36 kick, 37 side stick, 38 acoustic snare, 39 clap, 40 electric snare, 42 closed hat, 46 open hat, and 49 crash. Bass is monophonic, MIDI 28 to 47, channel 4. Primary sequence is monophonic, MIDI 55 to 84, channel 0. Secondary sequence is monophonic, MIDI 48 to 79, channel 1. Motif is monophonic, MIDI 60 to 86, channel 2. Harmonic field allows four notes, MIDI 45 to 76, channel 3. C4 is 60.
seed_meaning: Seeds identify kits. Nothing is random.
stack_warning: Use either the combined arrangement or the separate parts. Do not stack the part files on top of the combined file.
